cards.vorderseite: Trigeminal neuralgia: surgical options and their profiles
cards.rueckseite:
- **Microvascular decompression** (usually **SCA**): 85–95% initial success, ~30% recurrence at 10 y, **no sensory loss**
- **Percutaneous rhizotomy** (RF thermocoagulation, glycerol, balloon microcompression): 90–95% initial, repeatable; numbness (most with RF), risk of anesthesia dolorosa, keratitis
- **Radiosurgery** (root entry zone): 80–95% after ~3 months latency, ~25% recurrence at 3 y

cards.vorderseite: Severe complications of percutaneous trigeminal rhizotomy
Hemifacial spasm: offending vessel, treatment and main risk
cards.rueckseite: Usually **AICA** compressing the facial nerve root exit zone. Botulinum toxin (effective, temporary) or **microvascular decompression** (> 80% resolution). Main surgical risk: **hearing loss (up to 10%)**.

cards.vorderseite: Parkinson disease: indication and targets for DBS
cards.rueckseite: Indication: **levodopa-responsive** patients with disabling **off periods and dyskinesias**. Targets: **STN** (generally preferred, ~10% better, allows levodopa reduction) or **GPi** (~40% motor, ~65% dyskinesia improvement).
**Ventral intermediate nucleus (Vim) of the thalamus**: DBS or thalamotomy (also radiosurgical / focused ultrasound), 80–90% improvement of contralateral tremor.
**GPi** DBS (or pallidotomy), ~40% improvement; primary generalized and cervical dystonia respond better than secondary forms.

- **Intrathecal baclofen pump** (~30% catheter complications; withdrawal can be life-threatening)
- **Selective dorsal rhizotomy** (lumbar, interrupts the afferent reflex arc)

cards.text: Drug-refractory epilepsy: failure of {{c1::≥ 2 adequate antiepileptic drugs}}; affects {{c2::20–30%}} of patients. Well-selected epilepsy surgery: ~{{c3::60%}} seizure-free/good outcome.
Anterior temporal lobectomy: resect up to {{c1::4.5 cm}} from the temporal tip on the dominant side (speech) and up to {{c2::6 cm}} on the nondominant side (visual pathways).

cards.rueckseite:
- **Drop attacks (atonic):** anterior ⅔ **corpus callosotomy** (~70% improvement)
- Refractory generalized seizures: callosotomy or **vagus nerve stimulation** (~50% of patients get ~50% reduction)
- Catastrophic hemispheric epilepsy (Rasmussen, Sturge–Weber, hemimegalencephaly): **hemispherectomy** (functional less morbid than anatomic)

Percutaneous **C1–C2** lesion of the **spinothalamic tract** → relief of **contralateral** pain (~85%, up to 1 year). Ideal for **unilateral cancer pain below C5**. Bilateral lesions risk **Ondine's curse** (sleep apnea).
Lesioning of the dorsal root entry zone for refractory **brachial plexus root avulsion pain** or end-zone pain after spinal cord injury (~65% benefit at 10 y).
**T2–T3** sympathectomy (thoracoscopic), nearly 100% success. Dividing the **stellate ganglion** causes **Horner syndrome**.

cards.vorderseite: Endoscopic third ventriculostomy: requirements and success
cards.rueckseite: For **obstructive** hydrocephalus. Third ventricle must be wide enough, basilar artery not pressed against the clivus. Success **60–90%**.

cards.text: Shunt failure: {{c1::25–40%}} in the first year, then about {{c2::5% per year}}; about {{c3::50%}} have failed by 5 years.

cards.vorderseite: Normal pressure hydrocephalus: triad and response to shunting
cards.rueckseite: Triad: **gait disturbance** (magnetic gait), **urinary incontinence**, **dementia** ("wet, wobbly, wacky"). Gait and incontinence respond best, dementia least. Overall ~⅓ improve, ⅓ stabilize, ⅓ no response. Better results with a known cause (SAH, trauma, infection).

Young obese women (F:M 4–8:1), headache + **papilledema** without hydrocephalus, **enlarged blind spot**. Severe visual loss in ~10% if untreated. Exclude **venous sinus thrombosis**.
Treatment: weight loss (~6% often curative), **acetazolamide**; surgery: serial LPs, **lumboperitoneal shunt**, **optic nerve sheath fenestration** (protects vision only).
